summary.text: A 53-year-old man with treatment-resistant schizophrenia (schizoaffective disorder bipolar type), hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and hypothyroidism, hospitalized or institutionalized several times a year since age 17, presented from his nursing home with poor impulse control, aggression, reacting to internal stimuli and hyperverbality after 2 weeks of medication nonadherence. He had previously been stable on clozapine 200 mg nightly, paliperidone palmitate IM 234 mg monthly and escitalopram 10 mg daily; baseline clozapine concentrations were not done.

On admission he was agitated, labile and aggressive; escitalopram was stopped, paliperidone palmitate was given 5 days early and clozapine was slowly retitrated. By day 12 he consistently refused all psychotropics, clozapine was discontinued on day 29 and paliperidone palmitate was accepted only on day 33. He became increasingly uncooperative, paranoid and hypersexual and needed 10 emergency antipsychotic doses over 2 weeks.

After consent he received haloperidol decanoate 150 mg IM on day 40 as a second LAI. By day 46 to 47 his thought process was less disorganized, speech more redirectable, aggression largely resolved, mood predominantly euthymic, and he needed 1 emergency antipsychotic in the next 2 weeks; oral haloperidol 10 mg was started on day 48 to facilitate discharge to a nursing home. Sexually inappropriate and bizarre behaviors and pacing persisted, no upper-extremity rigidity was found, no adverse side effects were noted, and he largely returned to baseline by day 51.
